meta_title: How to Fight a Traffic Ticket in Alberta (2026) | Fabsy
meta_description: Dispute an Alberta traffic ticket before the printed deadline. Learn how pleas, disclosure, resolution, trial, and agent representation work.
h1: How to Fight a Traffic Ticket in Alberta
hook: To dispute an Alberta traffic ticket, follow the response instructions before the deadline printed on it and review the available evidence before choosing how to proceed.
bullets: Use the response deadline printed on the ticket.
Paying a ticket is a guilty plea: the conviction and any demerits are added to your driving record.
Available disclosure may include officer notes, device records, or video relevant to the allegation.
The applicable process and attendance requirements depend on the ticket and court.
A dispute may resolve or may proceed to trial, depending on the matter.
what:
What disputing a ticket means

Start with the notice itself. Confirm the alleged offence, response instructions, court office, and deadline printed on the ticket. Keep the original and any records related to the event.

A conviction can add demerits to your driving record. Speeding carries 2 to 6 demerits depending on how far over the limit you were. Suspension starts at 15 demerits for a full licence and 8 for a GDL. The effect depends on the offence and your existing driving record.
how:
How the dispute process works

  • Step 1: Check your deadline. Use the response date printed on the ticket.
  • Step 2: Follow the dispute instructions. File through the channel listed on the ticket, or have an agent assist where representation is permitted.
  • Step 3: Request disclosure. Available material may include officer notes, device records, calibration logs, or video. Review it before choosing how to proceed.
  • Step 4: Resolve or go to trial. The available path depends on the allegation, the evidence, and the court process. At trial, the Crown must prove the offence beyond a reasonable doubt.
next:
What to do right now

Photograph both sides of your ticket, note the printed deadline, and keep any relevant records. Send it to Fabsy for a free assessment of service eligibility and available next steps.

Pricing is a flat $488 plus 30% of any fine reduction achieved; there is no additional charge if the fine is not reduced.

faqs.q: How do I fight a traffic ticket in Alberta?
faqs.a: Follow the dispute instructions before the response deadline printed on your ticket, request the available disclosure, and review whether the matter may resolve or proceed to trial. An agent may assist where representation is permitted.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a traffic ticket in Alberta?
faqs.a: Use the response deadline printed on your ticket and follow the instructions on the notice. Act as soon as the ticket is in your hands.

faqs.q: Is it worth disputing a traffic ticket in Alberta?
faqs.a: It can be worth reviewing the evidence and possible driving-record impact before deciding how to respond. The available outcome depends on the allegation, the evidence, and the circumstances.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court to fight my ticket?
faqs.a: Attendance requirements depend on the charge, the court, and what happens in the matter. An agent can explain whether representation is permitted and tell you if personal attendance is required.

faqs.q: What happens if I just pay the ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea. The conviction goes on your driving abstract with any demerits, so review the ticket and your options before deciding how to respond.

faqs.q: How much does Fabsy charge to fight a ticket?
faqs.a: Pricing is a flat $488 plus 30% of any fine reduction achieved; there is no additional charge if the fine is not reduced.

faqs.q: Can the Crown just drop my ticket?
faqs.a: The Crown may withdraw or amend a charge, but whether that happens depends on the allegation, the evidence, and the circumstances. Review disclosure before choosing how to proceed.
